title: Introduce invocation-context heatmap, metric synthesis, and alert-decay orchestrator
author: Priya Nambiar
release_notes: Adds an invocation-context heatmap visualization + backend metric synthesis pipeline and an alert-decay orchestrator to reduce noisy alert churn. Backwards compatible; safe rollout via feature flag.
description:
Motivation: Oncall teams reported high alert churn from token-cost and latency spikes that were often contextual (same prompt shapes, but different tenant cohorts). This PR introduces a cross-layer observability flow: 1) a compact invocation-context heatmap that aggregates token-cost and phase-latency breakdowns by prompt-shape cohorts, 2) a metric-synthesis pipeline that joins sampled traces and sparse metrics to produce cohort-level rollups, and 3) an alert-decay orchestrator that automatically attenuates repeated low-signal alerts for cohorts that have transient short-lived bursts.

Summary of changes: - backend/telemetry: new metric_synthesis service that consumes sampled traces + token summaries and emits cohort rollups (sparklines, percentiles, burst counts) - observability/heatmap: new renderer and JSON dashboard definition for context-cohort heatmaps and sparklines - alerts/decay: orchestrator that tracks alert recurrence per-cohort and applies exponential decay to alert priority and notification channels - sdk/annotations: small additions to the trace annotation API to add cohort keys (prompt-shape hash, tenant-seg) - console: new per-route toggle to enable cohort rollups and an opt-in to run the decay orchestrator - tests: unit + e2e replaybench for synthetic bursts and alert-suppression behavior.

Design notes: The metric_synthesis service performs a streaming join between sampled OpenTelemetry spans (1:100 reservoir) and low-cardinality token summaries. We chose a time-windowed map-reduce style rollup with bounded memory by evicting cohort entries using an LRU with TTL and emitting downsampled sketches (t-digest for latency, weighted hist for token-cost). The heatmap UI renders cohorts along Y (prompt-shape clusters) and time on X, with stacked bars for phase-level latency and a sparkline for token-cost. The alert-decay orchestrator keeps a small state-per-cohort and reduces alert severity for noisy, quick-resolve bursts while escalating persistent regressions.

Compatibility and rollout: All new infra is behind feature flags: feature.cohort_rollups and feature.alert_decay. Default is off for all customers. Rollout plan: enable on internal staging (Nov 8), then opt-in beta for 5 customers (Nov 10), full behind-flag release (Nov 12).

Testing and verification: - unit tests for metric_synthesis aggregator and decay policy - replaybench end-to-end with synthetic invocation traces that exercise bursty and persistent patterns - manual verification of heatmap rendering with sampled datasets - CI smoke runs activated in pipeline.

Checklist: - [x] metric_synthesis service implemented - [x] heatmap dashboard JSON added - [x] orchestrator logic + graceful backoff added - [x] SDK trace annotations added - [x] tests + bench added - [x] docs + runbook (observability runbook) updated

Impact: This change reduces alert noise for short-lived token/latency bursts and surface higher fidelity cohort-level regressions to SRE. Expected net CPU/RAM for metric_synthesis: small (single-node staging) — we tuned defaults conservatively.
